pairs.subject: ci-execution-trust
pairs.evidence: src/features/plugins/gitlab/components/GitLabAgentList.tsx:129 Deploying with 'provision credentials' copies decrypted vault secrets into long-lived GitLab project CI/CD variables, but undeploying (this button, through gitlabSlice.gitlabUndeployAgent) never calls gitlab_revoke_credentials. That command has no caller outside the store slice, so the pipeline secrets outlive the deployment and are never cleaned up.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/gitlab.rs:257 Vault secrets become stored project-level pipeline variables with no owner, expiry or rotation, and no cleanup is wired to undeploy. The standard asks for fetch-at-step, short-lived credentials and named cleanup.

src-tauri/src/gitlab/converter.rs:116 Values that GitLab cannot mask are still pushed, just unmasked, so a job log can print them. This breaks 'assume every log line is disclosed'. The variables are protected:true (converter.rs:123), which keeps them out of unprotected merge-request pipelines and is a partial mitigation.

src/features/plugins/gitlab/hooks/usePipelineNotifications.ts:48 Pipeline statuses only feed notifications and a viewer for a person to read. No gate here merges or proves a change from a run, so 'latest run' is acceptable per the technique's when-not-to-use clause.

pairs.registryProposal: secret-materialization-discipline could name the case where a desktop app copies a local vault secret into a CI platform's stored variables: that copy is a second credential-delivery mechanism whose cleanup must be tied to the deployment's lifecycle.
